text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's monthly inflation slowed to 0.8 percent in June from 5.6 percent in May, National Statistics Institute figures showed.

-- Bulgaria's State Fund For Reconstruction and Development will place guarantees worth some 260 billion levs with Bulgarian commercial banks to cover credits to state firms for wheat purchases this year, Finance Minister Muravei Radev said.
-- Bulgaria will seek a 60 million Ecu loan from the European Investment Bank for the reconstruction of Sofia Airport, Transport Minister Wilhelm Kraus said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet raised foreign investment registration fees to 30,000 levs from 3.000 levs, the government press centre said.
-- State carrier Balkan Airlines said it had rescheduled by one year its debts amounting $15 million to the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development.
-- South Korea's Daewoo and Canada's Stellar Global Corporation have bid for a 57 percent stake in state fertiliser producer Chimko, the Privtisation Agency said.
-- Bulgaria's currency board system anchoring the lev to the mark will benefit from the mark's weakness against the dollar, central bank board member Rumen Avramov said.
-- The European Union is expected to extend a 250 million Ecu macroeconomic loan to Bulgaria by the end of this year, visiting European Commission unit leader Jean Trestour said.
-- Bulgaria's population is expected to fall to about seven million by 2020 because of low birth rate, economic crisis and high emigration, the National Statistics Institute said.

-- Bulgaria's parliament elected Stefan Dimitrov as director of the state national television and Lilyana Popova as director of the state national radio. Parliament is expected to elect today Panayot Denev as chief of the state BTA news agency. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145
